data.name: Mahakaleshwar
data.long_meaning: Mahakaleshwar is a name of Lord Shiva, the god of destruction and regeneration in Hinduism. The name Mahakaleshwar signifies the great time-keeper and destroyer of illusions and ignorance.
data.spiritual_meaning: Mahakaleshwar represents the divine power of destruction and transformation, and is a symbol of spiritual strength and wisdom.

in_sanskrit.name: महाकाल
in_sanskrit.long_meaning: Mahakala (Sanskrit: महाकाल, IAST: Mahākāla) is a Hindu deity, a form of Lord Shiva, and the god of time and the cosmic procession of time. The name is derived from Maha, meaning great, and Kala, meaning time.

vedic_reference.note: Mahakaleshwar is a significant deity in Hinduism and is mentioned in various Hindu scriptures such as the Mahabharata and the Puranas.

data.cultural_impact: Mahakaleshwar is a revered deity, especially in India where his temples are spread across various regions. One of the most famous temples dedicated to Mahakaleshwar is located in Ujjain, Madhya Pradesh. The annual Mahakala Jatara festival is a significant cultural event attracting thousands of pilgrims. Mahakaleshwar is also an important deity in Jainism, and the Ujjain temple is a popular site for pilgrimages for both Hindus and Jains.
data.spiritual_significance: Mahakaleshwar represents the domination of the divine consciousness over the material world. As a destroyer, he eliminates ignorance and illusions, allowing individuals to attain spiritual enlightenment. His iconography includes the Lingam symbol, which signifies the unmanifested and indestructible God. Mahakaleshwar's worship enables devotees to turn inward, focus on the self, and realize the ultimate reality. Ultimately, in this representation, he encourages spiritual growth and a deeper connection with the divine.
